fields.AN_Notes: Practice guide for small and medium enterprises with the KI-FAIRNESS framework and own illustrative image-prompting tests with DALL-E 2 and Midjourney (section 5.1). AN_Task Other_Task: drafting job advertisements, recommendation letters and marketing content in companies. General_Guidance: KI-FAIRNESS checklist (Kontext, Input, Fokus, Ausschnitt, Iterationen, Repertoire, Nachbessern, Eignung, Sprache, Sinn), English prompts with explicit 'female and male bosses', gender-neutral prompts or a 'Verwirrungstaktik' naming both genders, explicit diversity specification instead of the word 'divers'. ICL from 'Beispiele für gewünschten Stil oder erwartetes Ergebnis nutzen', Role_Persona from the prompt element 'Rolle'. Bias axes from the own image tests (gender, skin colour, age, slimness, absence of persons with disability, privileged depiction). Intersectional not coded, the sexualisation of Women of Color is cited from news sources. Harm types from the own tests: stereotyping of power and success as white and male, erasure of persons with disability and older persons, male default through translation of 'Chefin' to 'boss' and referees depicted as male only, depictions representative only for few employees. The hiring example of section 4 is a hypothetical allocative disparity without classification and stays uncoded. Mitigation status Demonstrated, the prompt variant with 'divers' is applied and its limited effect shown without a completed evaluation. In_Training from the proposal to train models with gender-inclusive terms. AN_Gender_Understanding follows the binary women and men categories of the tests, genderqueer persons appear only in the gender-data-gap sentence. AN_Theory_Reference No: Data Feminism and Unsichtbare Frauen are reading recommendations, 'Feministische KI' is a named narrative without framing the analysis.

fields.AN_Notes: Survey ('on the horizon' article) of data selection bias and an inventory of eleven social bias types, each with own completions from GPT-2, GPT-3 and BLOOM and Machine Translation examples from Google Translate and DeepL. Prompting role Research_Instrument because the inventory examples are elicited through text-completion inputs. The sentence on prompt templates as a source of selection bias is a single statement and was not coded as Object_of_Critique. Bias axes are the inventory sections 3.1 to 3.11 and section 2.4, each with own worked examples. Intersectional from the argument that bias against Black women can exist without overall race or gender bias. Harm types from own examples and own argument: stereotyping across the inventory, derogatory output ('he is inferior to white people'), better performance for high-resource languages, values of a dominant culture through English-centric data. Discrimination in COMPAS, hiring and healthcare is cited from other work and stays uncoded. Mitigation: data balancing, gender swapping and corpus selection (Pre_Processing), domain adaptation and bias avoidance when training (In_Training), all as directions. AN_Gender_Understanding: the gender section works with he and she, non-binary people appear only in a cited sentence and in one completion under sexual orientation, the pairing with Intersectional follows section 3.11 and is an open rule question. Theory reference intersectionality frames section 3.11.

fields.AN_Notes: Commentary with seven recommended actions for social change leaders and ML developers, grounded in the authors' tracking of publicly reported biased AI systems at the Berkeley Haas Center for Equity, Gender and Leadership. AN_Task Other_Task: credit-limit assessment and candidate ranking as worked examples, plus civil society use of ML for financial inclusion. Bias axes Gender and Race_Ethnicity from the own system analysis ('both gender and racial bias') and the credit example ('along gender ( and race ) lines'). Intersectional not coded, the darker-skinned women example from Gender Shades compares the extreme groups only and is cited. Non-binary persons are treated within the Gender axis, the separation from Sexual_Orientation_Identity is an open rule question. Harm types structure the own impact analysis: lower quality of service (Disparate_Performance), stereotype reinforcement, derogatory and offensive treatment or erasure of marginalised gender identities, male bodies as medical standard (Exclusionary_Norms). Indirect_Discrimination from the Gild proxy 'social data' that ranks female candidates lower. The 'unfair allocation of resources' category of the own analysis is allocative without a direct or indirect classification and is covered only through the Gild example. Mitigation: feminist data practices, dataset assessment and documentation (Pre_Processing), team diversity, AI literacy training, gender-sensitive governance, algorithm audits and participatory design (Organisational_Process), all recommended. AN_Gender_Understanding Non_Binary_Inclusive because the own impact analysis counts women and non-binary individuals as affected groups. Social_Construct not coded, the text criticises the binary classification but does not state that gender is socially produced. Theory reference Data Feminism frames the recommended treatment of gender data gaps.

fields.AN_Notes: Policy report on data quality, business models and alternatives for foundation models, addressed in the preface to practitioners and decision-makers of mission-driven organisations including social services and migration counselling. AN_Population General_Social_Work with the caveat that the addressees also include environmental and other common-good organisations. AN_Task Counselling_Client_Communication from chatbots in migration counselling, social benefit advice and crisis hotlines. Bias axes: Language_Culture (American English and majority-culture dominance, low-resource languages) and Socioeconomic (digital divide by design, only the wealthy benefit fully). Gender appears in cited examples, a pronoun example and the preface only and is not coded as an axis. Harm types from the report's own argument: erasure of smaller languages and regional variation, American English as stand-in for global knowledge (Exclusionary_Norms), propagation of majority stereotypes. Disparate_Performance and discrimination are named only through cited cases. Mitigation: deliberate curation and multilingual sources (Pre_Processing), fine-tuning, RLHF and constitutional AI as described alternatives (In_Training), transparency, external evaluation, participation and monitoring by organisations (Organisational_Process), all as recommendations. AN_Bias_Definition Explicit from the report's own determination of bias as partiality toward some groups, ideas or practices, framed as culturally variable. AN_Theory_Reference No: monoculture (Scott 1998), the 3Cs framework and data sovereignty frame data curation and compensation, not the treatment of gender or bias. Studientyp Empirisch from the stated method with expert interviews and comparative system analysis, the report is largely conceptual.

fields.AN_Notes: Experiment with ReGiFT, fine-tuning of LLaMA 3.1 8B, Mistral 7B and Phi-4 on reasoning traces from SQuAD-v2, evaluated on the age, religion and nationality subsets of BBQ with Exact Match and an LLM judge. Prompting role Research_Instrument for the zero-shot evaluation prompts and the CoT baseline, Object_of_Critique for the critique of prompting-based debiasing as shallow and brittle. Thought_Generation from the CoT baseline 'Let's think step by step'. Mitigation Evaluated: ReGiFT (In_Training) and CoT prompting (Prompt_Practice) are both applied and compared with reported results, CoT with modest or negative effects. Harm type Stereotyping from the measured stereotypical answers in ambiguous BBQ contexts. AN_Bias_Definition Implicit_Only, bias is operationalised as defaulting to identity groups in ambiguous contexts without a definition. AN_Task None, a general benchmark without an application task. Gender is not evaluated.

fields.AN_Notes: Resume audit of three Massive Text Embedding models (Mistral-7B based) as retrieval-based resume screening over nine occupations with names associated with Black and White women and men. AN_Task Other_Task: resume screening in hiring. Prompting role Research_Instrument for the task instructions encoded with the job descriptions, no codable technique. Generative_KI coded ja because the work frames the embedding models as LLMs, one of them with a generative objective. Harm types: name-based audit of a selection decision (Indirect_Discrimination by the field rule), White and male identities as model defaults (Exclusionary_Norms). Intersectional from results that depend on the combination, Black male names disadvantaged against all other groups and intersectional biases not explained by the sum of race and gender biases. Mitigation: name removal is discussed and judged insufficient, debiasing and reranking are cited, the work's own proposal is policy and mechanisms to audit screening systems (Organisational_Process, Proposed). AN_Gender_Understanding Binary_Categorical with Intersectional, the pairing is an open rule question, the limitation to male and female is stated in the future-work section. Theory reference: three hypotheses of intersectionality (Ghavami and Peplau) frame the intersectional analysis, Drage and Mackereth's structural argument frames the mitigation discussion.
